title: Meta says 'reevaluating' 2030 net zero target amid AI buildout
summary: Meta said Thursday it was reconsidering its 2030 deadline for net zero emissions because of the artificial intelligence boom, the latest in a broad retreat by corporations on global warming targets. The reality has been far more complex," the executives wrote, adding that delivering on Meta's vision "requires building the infrastructure that powers AI." In 2020, Meta set a goal of net zero emissions across its entire value chain by the year 2030, in order to align with the Paris Agreement, which seeks to hold long-term warming to 1.5C to avert climate catastrophes.
llm_summary: Meta announced it is re‑examining its pledge to hit net‑zero emissions across its whole value chain by 2030, citing the rapid expansion of AI as a complicating factor. The company says the “reality has been far more complex” and that meeting its climate goals now hinges on building the massive infrastructure needed to power AI workloads. This move reflects a broader trend of tech firms reassessing earlier climate targets.
